audit_result.proof_trace: The `postgres_changes` Realtime subscription is established using the public anon key (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) with no Supabase auth context, meaning Supabase evaluates RLS for the `anon` Postgres role. For the subscription to deliver events to the kiosk at all, the `anon` role must have SELECT access to `attendance.temp_registrations` — the same access any external client with the public anon key can exploit to subscribe to any known `qrToken`. The codebase provides no enforcement; correctness depends entirely on Supabase RLS configuration that cannot be verified from source and has been historically misconfigured in this repo.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An attacker near the kiosk observes or photographs the QR code displayed on screen (obtaining the `qr_<UUID>` token), then opens a Supabase Realtime connection with the public anon key and subscribes to `kiosk-qr-channel-<stolen-token>` to receive UPDATE events on the victim's `temp_registrations` row, leaking `accessed_at` timestamps and `is_used` state changes in real-time.

PROP-e5782b58-asm-008.text: Supabase Realtime subscriptions must enforce RLS; unauthenticated clients must not receive events.
PROP-e5782b58-asm-008.assertion: forall realtime_subscription: RLS policies applied to broadcast events
